plainport 0.1.0-dev: offload, onload and move coding projects

Usage: plainport <command> [options]

Projects:
  ls         read        Every project with its root, state, device, size and last activity
  status     read        One project in detail: its state, head, lease and what to do next
  offload    confirm     Snapshot a project, verify it and free its folder; --dry-run shows the plan first
  onload     safe_write  Restore a shelved project into place and reinstall its dependencies
  hydrate    safe_write  Install a project's dependencies again with its own package manager (frozen)
  dehydrate  safe_write  Remove a project's installed dependencies (only what a plugin claims and git does not track)
  restore    safe_write  Restore a snapshot side by side into a free path: no lease, no hydration

Recovery and cleanup:
  recover    safe_write  Settle interrupted operations: roll back what had not committed, finish what had
  gc         safe_write  Delete released trash past its keepLocalFor deadline; --now deletes it early

Roots:
  root add   safe_write  Add a root, optionally with this device's folder for it; the global --store sets its store
  root bind  safe_write  Point a root at its folder on this device
  root list  read        Show every root, its folder on each device and its state here
  root scan  safe_write  Find every project under a root's folder here and register the new ones

Setup and info:
  help       read        Show every command, or one command's arguments, options and risk class
  init       confirm     Name this device, set up its roots and record the store snapshots go to
  version    read        Print plainport's version

Global options:
  --json           Print NDJSON: event lines, then exactly one final envelope
  --yes            Allow a confirm-class command to run; --plan <id> stands in for it on a command that runs a --dry-run's plan
  --no-input       Never prompt; implied when stdin is not a terminal
  --dry-run        Preview only: build and print the plan, change nothing
  --store <name>   Use this store instead of the default
  --config <path>  Read this config file instead of the default
  --quiet          Print only results, warnings and errors
  --verbose        Print debug logs too

read and safe_write commands run freely; confirm commands need --yes, or --plan <id> with the id their --dry-run
printed. --dry-run always runs as read.
Run plainport help <command> for a command's arguments, options and examples.
For scripts and agents: add --json to any command for NDJSON with one final envelope; plainport help --json lists
the commands as data; plainport.json, generated from the same registry, is the full machine contract (every
schema, exit code and finding) and is large: read it as data, not as help.
